entries.note: ML Atlas's evaluation-metrics module ran into its first mid-batch cutoff — an agent finished all its research and verification but got cut off right before writing the lesson file. Finished it by hand, reusing its already-verified work.
Built the public Q&A box on this page: type a question, it opens a GitHub Issue, gets checked and answered here automatically.

Answered the first two questions asked here — added the concept number next to the module number, and fixed a real bug where the 'live status' line was showing an hours-old stale update instead of just going quiet.

RAG Atlas's math module hit a bigger cutoff cascade across one batch — one lesson had even been written in the wrong state (marked 'complete' while it was still the newest one). Fixed the state bug and manually finished the two lessons that never got written.
Finished ML Atlas's Goodhart's-law lesson by hand after its batch run also got cut off right before writing it.
Launched the closing two-lesson batches for both courses' current modules.

Split the GitHub-checking job into a fast 2-minute poll (just for new questions) and a slower 17-minute one (build health) — the fast one wasn't getting a chance to run during long back-and-forth conversations.
Redesigned the how-it-works page with real numbers and a step-by-step layout instead of generic description, per a question asked here.
Added this activity feed so what's actually happening shows up here, instead of needing to be asked in chat.

Answered two more questions from here — why 'researching' takes so long (real network calls + hand-checked math, every lesson), and added a matching how-it-built page to the RAG Atlas site itself, not just this dashboard.

RAG Atlas Module 07, Concept 02 (Fixed-size and recursive chunking): the write step got throttled by the API and silently retried a second time. Took over manually rather than wait out the retry — finished the lesson by hand from the already-verified research plan.

Same pattern hit RAG Atlas Concept 04 (Semantic and proposition-based chunking) — a second attempt was already running with no result yet. Stopped it and finished the lesson by hand again, same as Concept 02.

Set up a dedicated monitoring agent that checks both courses every 5 minutes, watches for exactly this retry pattern in the build logs, and takes over automatically-detected stalls before they waste 20+ minutes silently.
